chapter_mission: Let the cost of the meeting hit, show the wound inside the group, and push Sera and Ben into the last stage of recognizing Torin.
chapter_turn: Torin stops reading as an ally with bad ideas and starts reading as someone already halfway gone.

scene_plan.purpose: Open with Desh proving the sabotage and the countdown becoming unavoidable.
Let a trivial argument show the wound amplifying what is already there, then have Kael ask the question nobody else will.
End on Veraine and Torin both orienting toward Veranthos in ways Ben can finally read.

relationship_turns.to: decided man — Torin's doorway announcement uses the specific cadence Jacen used before the worst conversations. Ben has the pattern now. The question is what he will do with it

stops defending — the sharp late break in the Sera/Torin arc (relocated from Ch 13 per D7). Sera's silence in response to Kael's question is the beat. Per D7 Component A, this is the second-loudest visible telegraph, concurrent with the Ch 17 s1 doorway announcement

the one who names the tension no one else will — W1 Inversion 2. Kael's question is the trigger for Sera's shift; he has now moved from adjacent to load-bearing in the group's ability to reach the Ch 21 decision
internal pressure — the amplification effect is in the room. Every argument will be louder than its subject from here on. The wound is pressurising the coalition from inside

working in concert — Desh's food delivery after the argument is the first time he acts as emotional infrastructure for the whole group, not just Ben's plus-one. His supporting presence lands as action

exit_vector: Two ships converging on Veranthos. Torin's silhouette in the cockpit viewport, reflection overlaid on a sensor dot that will arrive when he does. Desh's countdown timer at hours. The group in their quarters with a pressure in their chests none of them can name. The second pinch point's clock is set. Sera has stopped defending; Kael has named; the room has changed.
notes: This chapter is pressure, not explanation. Keep the sabotage, the argument, and the sensor-dot closing movement tied together.
